reasoning_traces.think:
The glocal framework integrates local and global explanation paradigms by aggregating per-shot SHAP values (aggregated SHAP) and marginal ceteris-paribus profiles (AP) over groups of observations. This allows soccer analysts to understand how collective performance metrics (e.g., team xG) arise from individual shot characteristics. The SHAP formulation assumes additivity, where each feature contributes independently to the outcome. In contrast, AP estimates marginal effects by holding all but one variable constant, which can be distorted by feature correlation. The framework's core insight lies in its ability to scale explanations from single events to group dynamics without losing fidelity to underlying model behavior. However, it suffers from computational complexity in aSHAP and sensitivity to correlated inputs in AP. These limitations mirror those in GSE’s EPA modeling, where feature interactions and temporal dependencies challenge interpretability. The framework thus provides a bridge between model introspection and operational decision-making.
